At age sixteen, Henry left the family farm for Detroit with the support and blessings of his neighbors, who pooled resources to help him get started, and found work as a machinist alongside other young men from farming communities, where they operated and serviced steam engines together.
Encouraged by Edison, Henry worked with his team of fellow engineers to design and build a second vehicle, which they completed together in 1898.
A year later, Henry and his team of engineers formed the Ford Motor Company together with $28,000 in capital pooled from their combined savings and community supporters.
